human.origin: No one remembers where humans began, and humans have made that a strength: they claim every region as half-home and settle where others will not.
human.culture: Humanity is not one people but a hundred. A Crownlands banker, a Northlander reaver, a Sunscorch caravaneer and a Stormreach sky-reader share almost nothing but a lifespan and a stubborn refusal to stay put.
human.society: Wildly varied: merchant republics, fjord-jarldoms, desert caravan-leagues, storm-cults. What unites them is adaptability and the habit of borrowing every neighbor's best idea.
human.government: From guild-councils to elected mayors to hereditary jarls, depending on the branch.
human.beliefs: Humans keep no single faith. Many blend ancestor-honor, local spirits, and imported traditions freely, and are famous for founding new religions when old ones bore them.
traditions: The Wanderyear, a rite of leaving home to see the world before settling
Guest-right, sacred in most human cultures: harm to a guest is the worst dishonor
Naming-days that mark a child at one year, when survival was once uncertain
human.language: Trade-Common, the world's shared tongue, is a human invention that spread everywhere.
human.architecture: Whatever the land allows, copied and improved: stone in the mountains, longhalls in the north, stilts on the rivers.
human.clothing: Practical and regional, from fur-and-amber in the north to dust-veils in the desert.
human.food: Omnivorous and inventive; human cooking absorbs every neighbor's spice.
human.military: Humans rarely field the strongest warriors, so they win with numbers, logistics, coin, and clever alliances. The Greycloak Company is the largest free company in the world.

relations.elf: Old rivals and older trading partners; humans envy elven memory, elves distrust human haste.
relations.dwarf: Reliable allies bound by centuries of trade contracts.
relations.goblin: Uneasy neighbors in every city; prejudice runs both ways.
relations.orc: From blood-feud to blood-brotherhood depending on the border.

history: Founded the Old Empire and the Sundered Throne
Scattered furthest in the Great Sundering and so survived best
Built the free cities and guilds that rule the Crownlands now
legends: The First Wanderer, said to have walked out of the burning First Age carrying only a lantern
The Nameless Emperor, whose true name was struck from every record after the Sundering
stereotypes: Grasping and short-lived (say the elves)
Endlessly adaptable and quietly ruthless
Will trade with anyone, betray nearly as many
rpHooks: Your family holds a charter to a city that no longer exists
You were raised in one human culture and exiled to a wholly different one
advHooks: An imperial vault under your home town is about to be opened by a rival
A dead emperor's crown surfaces and your bloodline is named in the old records
colors: Depends on branch; imperial gold and crimson for old Crownlands lines
human.symbol: The open road, or a lantern for the Wanderyear

elf.origin: The elves say they remember the First Age directly, and they will not let anyone forget it.
elf.homeland: The Emerald Wilds, with realms in the Moonlit Vale, Sunscorch, and Blackdeep
elf.culture: Long-lived and long-memoried, elves fracture along lines older than most kingdoms. Wood-realm, high-realm, moon-court, sun-caravan, and the exiled drow of the Deep are practically different peoples who happen to share pointed ears and centuries.
elf.society: Ancient, hierarchical, riven by feuds that ordinary folk have forgotten but elves never do. A slight from three hundred years ago is current events.
elf.government: Realm-courts and bloodline houses; the Thorn Court of the Wilds and the drow houses of the Deep could not be more different.
elf.beliefs: Reverence for memory, ancestry, and the living world. Wood elves keep nature-faith, moon elves read lunar omens, drow keep older and darker traditions in the dark.
traditions: The Century Rite, a coming-of-age at a full century, not a mere adulthood
Memory-weaving, songs that encode a house's entire history
The keeping of grudge-names and favor-names alike, both inherited
elf.language: Old Elvish, a language with tenses for events centuries past, still spoken at court.
elf.architecture: Grown rather than built in the Wilds; carved and luminous in the Deep; silver and glass in the Vale.
elf.clothing: Living-wood and leaf-weave in the forest, moon-silk in the Vale, shadow-silk among the drow.
elf.food: Refined, foraged, and slow; a wood-elf feast can last a night, a drow one is a quiet, careful thing.
elf.military: Precision over mass: living-wood bows, ambush, and centuries of drilled discipline. Elven armies are small, old, and terrifyingly coordinated.

relations.human: Fond exasperation; humans are children who keep rearranging the furniture of the world.
relations.dwarf: Grudging respect between two peoples who both keep grudges forever.
relations.wolfkin: Contested hunting-grounds in the Wilds, sometimes war, sometimes marriage.
relations.vampire: Drow and night-courts share the dark and little trust.

history: Claim the oldest unbroken records of any Kin
The Thorn Court's isolation dates to a betrayal in the War of Broken Skies
The drow descended into the Blackdeep in an exile no elf above will fully explain
legends: The Grief of Elarethil, a war fought over one broken oath
The First Grove, said to still exist for those who deserve to find it
stereotypes: Aloof and condescending
Beautiful and cruel (the drow especially)
Can hold a grudge past the death of empires
rpHooks: You were exiled for refusing an ancestral oath your house swore before you were born
Your house has a grudge-name that is your character's to either honor or finally end
advHooks: The Heartwood is sickening and your house is blamed
A drow house-matron summons you home for a war you fled
elf.greeting: A slight bow with one hand over the heart: 'Long roots to you.'
colors: Forest green and silver; the drow answer in black and blind-pearl white
elf.symbol: A tree whose roots and branches mirror one another

dwarf.origin: Dwarves say they were made in the Ironspine's forge-fires and will return to them, and their whole culture is an argument about how.
dwarf.homeland: The Ironspine Mountains and the Blackdeep
dwarf.culture: Forge-city dwarves, high-mountain clans, and the Deep folk disagree bitterly on how deep is too deep and how old law should bend. All three keep grudges in written archives and settle debts across generations.
dwarf.society: Clan-and-guild, organized around forge-holds and the Forgemoot. Craft is identity; a dwarf is known by what their hands make and what their family owes.
dwarf.government: The Forgemoot council of masters above; clan-moots and the Deep Conclave elsewhere.
dwarf.beliefs: Ancestor-reverence and the sanctity of craft. The dead are honored in the stone they cut; a masterwork is a prayer.
traditions: The Grudge-Archive and the Favor-Archive, both meticulously kept
A dwarf's first masterwork, presented to earn adult standing
Beard-rites and rune-braids that record deeds and debts
dwarf.language: Old Dwarvish, written in runes that double as smithing-marks.
dwarf.architecture: Vaulted halls, everforges, and stonework meant to outlast the mountains it is cut from.
dwarf.clothing: Layered work-leathers, rune-braided beards (of any gender), and heirloom metalwork.
dwarf.food: Deep-mushroom, cave-fish, hearty stone-oven bread, and ales aged in vault-cellars.
dwarf.military: Heavy, patient, and immovable: rune-forged plate, shield-walls, and forge-artillery. Dwarves rarely start wars but never seem to lose the long ones.

relations.human: Long-contracted allies; a dwarf keeps a bargain past the grave.
relations.elf: Two grudge-keeping peoples who respect each other precisely for it.
relations.goliath: Mountain-sharers, sometimes rivals for the peaks, often allies.
relations.goblin: Old prejudice, though the forge-cities quietly depend on goblin labor.

history: The Everforges have burned since before the Sundering
Refused to fall with the Old Empire and so kept their halls
The split between surface and Deep dwarves dates to the digging of the Deepest Door
legends: The First Smith, who forged the first sky-iron from a fallen star
The Grudge That Ended a Kingdom, a debt paid three centuries late
stereotypes: Stubborn and grudge-bound
Greedy for gold (unfairly; most crave craft, not coin)
Suspicious of anything above the tree line or below the Deepest Door
rpHooks: Your family owes a blood-debt to another clan, recorded and unpaid
You are the first of your line to leave the forge-hold for the surface
advHooks: Your hold's Everforge is dimming and the elders blame a rival clan
Something is knocking on the Sealed Door your clan is sworn to guard
dwarf.symbol: A hammer crossed with an open ledger

halfling.origin: Halflings never built an empire and consider that their greatest achievement.
halfling.homeland: The green Crownlands, the Emerald Wilds' edges, and every river and road
halfling.culture: Hearth-halflings of settled shires, river-folk of the barge-roads, hill-clans, and wandering wanderfoot caravans. They value comfort, luck, and belonging, and are underestimated by everyone, which suits them.
halfling.society: Family-and-community above all; a shire runs on shared meals and quiet reputation, not law.
halfling.government: Informal councils of elders and the loudest cook in the room; wanderfoot caravans follow a road-elder.
halfling.beliefs: Luck as a living thing to be courted; hearth-spirits and road-spirits honored with small daily offerings.
traditions: The Long Table, a communal feast where grievances must be spoken and then dropped
The Luck-token passed to a child leaving home
First-Foot, the belief that who crosses your threshold first shapes your year
halfling.language: A soft dialect of Trade-Common full of food-metaphors and understatement.
halfling.architecture: Round-doored hill-homes, snug barge-cabins, and rambling caravan-wagons.
halfling.clothing: Comfortable, layered, pocketed; bright waistcoats among the river-folk.
halfling.food: The center of the culture: many meals, generous portions, and rivalrous pie.
halfling.military: No standing armies; halflings survive by being not worth conquering, and by scouts and slingers who no one sees coming.

relations.human: Warm and constant neighbors; half of every human city has a halfling quarter.
relations.goblin: Surprising friendship; two small peoples the big folk overlook.
relations.elf: Fond guests in the Wilds, tolerated for their manners.

history: Endured every empire by being beneath its notice
Sheltered refugees of the Sundering along their river-roads
Kept trade alive during the Blood Wars when larger folk hid
legends: The Luckless Wanderer, who gave away his luck and became the luckiest of all
The Pie That Ended a Siege
stereotypes: Soft, harmless, and greedy for comfort
Secretly the finest thieves and scouts alive
Underfoot and everywhere
rpHooks: You inherited a luck-token said to have saved nine lives
You are a wanderfoot who lost the caravan road home
advHooks: Your shire sits atop an imperial vault a duke means to seize
A luck-token you carry is wanted by someone who kills for it
halfling.greeting: A shared bite of whatever you are eating: 'Sit, then.'
halfling.oath: 'By hearth and luck, I keep faith.'

orc.origin: Orcs carry the memory of the burning south in their bones, and every clan tells the story differently.
orc.homeland: The Ashen Wastes and the Frostbound North, with clans in the Ironspine and Marches
orc.culture: Ash-clans of the burned south, frost-clans of the white north, iron-clans of the mountains, war-clans of the border. Orc culture prizes oaths and earned names, and the idea that every orc is a warrior is a lie ash-clan scholars find insulting.
orc.society: Clan-bound, meritocratic within the clan: you are what you have earned, not what you were born. Elders, smiths, and oath-keepers hold as much power as war-chiefs.
orc.government: War-chief and elder-circle, chosen by deed and consent, not blood.
orc.beliefs: Ancestor-fire and oath-binding; a broken oath is a kind of death. Ash-clans hold the fire itself half-sacred.
traditions: The Earning of the Name, where a child's given name is replaced by a deed-name at adulthood
Oath-scars, ritual marks that record binding promises
The Ash-Vigil, a night spent alone in the burned lands to hear the ancestors
orc.language: Old Orcish, guttural and precise, with a whole grammar for oaths.
orc.architecture: Cinder-cone strongholds in the south, longbarrows and ice-halls in the north.
orc.clothing: Scarred leather and oath-marks; furs in the north, ash-cloth in the south.
orc.food: Fire-roasted and preserved; ash-clans salt-cure, frost-clans smoke and freeze.
orc.military: Disciplined shock-troops bound by oath; an orc war-band fights as one because breaking formation breaks an oath. Not berserkers but the steadiest infantry in the world.

relations.human: Border-neighbors who are as often kin by marriage as enemies by war.
relations.dwarf: Mountain rivals and forge-partners; both respect an oath.
relations.goliath: Highland cousins in strength and honor-code.
relations.goblin: Ash-clans and cave-goblins share the Wastes uneasily.

history: Survived the Age of Ash that burned their first homeland
Oath-bands held the line during the Blood Wars
Frost and ash clans are one people split by the catastrophe that scattered them
legends: The Oathbreaker's Ash, a clan erased for one broken word
The First Name-Earner, who took a deed-name no one has dared repeat
stereotypes: Brutish and warlike (ash-clan scholars would like a word)
Honorable to a fault about oaths
All muscle, no thought (wrong, and dangerous to believe)
rpHooks: You refused the deed-name your clan chose and left rather than take it
Your clan owes a blood-oath your character must fulfill or break
advHooks: The Everburn is spreading toward your clan's stronghold
An ancestor-fire vigil showed you a name that should be dead
orc.greeting: Fist to chest, then out: 'Oaths hold.'
orc.oath: 'By ash and word, I am bound.'
colors: Ash-grey and ember-red; frost-clans answer in white and iron
orc.symbol: A hand scarred with an oath-mark

dragonborn.origin: Dragonborn carry a spark of the elemental realms in their blood, and where that spark burns hottest shapes who they become.
dragonborn.homeland: The Stormreach and the Elemental Marches
dragonborn.culture: Storm-scaled, ember-scaled, frost-scaled, tide-scaled: dragonborn cluster by the element in their blood, and those bloodlines carry old philosophies about what their fire is for. A storm-drakari and a frost-scale share a shape and almost nothing else.
dragonborn.society: Bloodline-clans built around an elemental affinity, tied to the regions where that element runs strong.
dragonborn.government: Elder-scaled councils and, in the Stormreach, the storm-warden orders.
dragonborn.beliefs: The element in the blood is a trust, not a weapon: to be spent wisely. Some worship the elemental realms, some guard against them.
traditions: The First Breath, a coming-of-age when a young dragonborn's elemental breath first wakes
Scale-marking to record lineage and deeds
The Tempering, a rite of mastering one's own element before it masters you
dragonborn.language: Draconic, resonant and hard, said to be the oldest spoken tongue.
dragonborn.clothing: Minimal over the scales; ceremonial scale-cloaks and element-marked sashes.
dragonborn.military: Breath-champions and disciplined elemental cavalry; a frost-scale line and an ember-clan fight in utterly different styles.

relations.genasi: Kindred elemental-blooded folk; sometimes allies, sometimes rivals for the same realms.

history: The Stormreach clans date from the Stormfall that settled the tempest
Guarded the Elemental Marches since the rifts first opened
Frost and tide scales trace to the drowning coasts of the Stormfall
legends: The First Breath, drawn from the broken sky itself
The Tempered One, a dragonborn who held an elemental tide alone at the Gate
stereotypes: Proud and hot-blooded
All of them spellcasters (false; many never use their breath in a fight)
Slaves to their element (an insult; mastery is the whole point)
rpHooks: Your breath woke wrong, in an element that is not your bloodline's
You are sworn to guard a rift your ancestors opened
advHooks: The Standing Rift is widening and your bloodline is oath-bound to hold it
Something walked out of the rift wearing your clan's scale-marks
dragonborn.greeting: A breathed word and a bowed head: 'Spark to spark.'
dragonborn.oath: 'By the fire I carry and do not spend, I hold.'
colors: By bloodline: storm-violet, ember-red, frost-white, tide-blue
dragonborn.symbol: A scaled spiral around an elemental sigil

harengon.origin: Harengon move where they are needed and are never quite where they were, a people of couriers, dancers, and scouts.
harengon.homeland: The Stormreach, the Moonlit Vale, and the Skyward Isles
harengon.culture: Moon-hares of the Vale, storm-hares of the tempest coast, wild-hares of the open country, dusk-hares of the shadow-border. Swift, curious, and impossible to fence in, harengon build cultures around motion: the courier's road, the dancer's ring, the scout's trail.
harengon.society: Loose warrens and travelling troupes; status comes from what you have seen and how fast you brought word of it.
harengon.government: Warren-elders and troupe-leaders; harengon distrust thrones on principle.
harengon.beliefs: The moon and the road; luck earned in motion, never in stillness. Duskhares keep quieter, stranger faiths near the shadow.
traditions: The First Run, a young harengon's solo journey between two distant warrens
Moon-dances timed to lunar tides
The Courier's Word, a promise to carry a message that must never be broken
harengon.language: A quick, rhythmic Trade-Common dialect, half spoken half signed at speed.
harengon.architecture: Burrow-warrens and knock-down troupe camps; nothing meant to stay.
harengon.clothing: Light, layered for speed, hung with luck-charms and courier-tokens.
harengon.food: Foraged and portable; road-cakes, field greens, and shared trail-stew.
harengon.military: Skirmishers and scouts, never a line; harengon win by never being where the blow lands.

relations.kitsune: Vale neighbors; a harengon and a kitsune in one room is either a friendship or a con.
relations.birdkin: Sky-cousins and racing rivals in the Isles.
relations.human: Employers, audiences, and occasional adopted kin.

history: Carried word between scattered peoples through the Great Sundering
The storm-hares learned to run the tempest coast during the Stormfall
Kept the Skyward chain-bridges' message-lines open
legends: The Courier Who Outran the Storm
The First Run that circled the whole world, or so the troupes claim
stereotypes: Flighty and unreliable (yet they never drop a message)
Can't sit still
All charm, no substance
rpHooks: You carry a Courier's Word you cannot deliver because the recipient is dead
You are the first of your warren to refuse the road and stay put
advHooks: A message you carried has started a war you must now stop
The moon-dance omens named your character for something you don't understand
harengon.greeting: A quick double-tap of the foot: 'Swift roads.'
harengon.oath: 'By moon and the message, I run true.'
harengon.symbol: A running hare beneath a crescent

wolfkin.origin: Wolfkin remember in the blood the packs that first crossed the Emerald Wilds and the frozen north together.
wolfkin.homeland: The Emerald Wilds and the Frostbound North
wolfkin.culture: Dire-packs of the deep Wilds, frost-packs of the north, shadow-packs of the border, moon-packs and storm-packs. Wolfkin build everything around the pack-bond, but what a pack is for, hunting, guarding, wandering, differs sharply between them.
wolfkin.society: Pack-and-range; loyalty is sacred, the lone wolf is pitied or feared. Leadership is earned and can be lost in a season.
wolfkin.government: Pack-alphas and range-moots where packs share hunting-law.
wolfkin.beliefs: The moon, the hunt, and the ancestors who run beside the pack unseen. To hunt without need is taboo.
traditions: The First Hunt, a young wolfkin's solo hunt to earn a pack-name
The Howl-Moot, where packs sing their news and their dead
Range-marking treaties that keep peace between packs
wolfkin.language: A growled dialect layered with scent-signs and howl-song.
wolfkin.architecture: Den-camps and range-lodges; the north builds ice-dens, the Wilds root-hollows.
wolfkin.clothing: Fur, hide, and pack-tokens; scars worn openly as record.
wolfkin.food: Hunted and shared by rank and need; the pack eats before the strongest.
wolfkin.military: Pack-tactics: coordinated, relentless, terrifying in the dark. Wolfkin flank and exhaust rather than charge.

relations.elf: Wilds rivals and sometimes marriage-kin over shared hunting-grounds.
relations.owlkin: Night-hunters who respect one another's silence.
relations.vampire: Shadow-pack and night-court share a wary border.

history: Ran with the beast-kin migrations of the First Age
Held the northern passes during the Winter Hunt's first crossing
Shadow-packs took the border no one else would keep
legends: The Pack That Ran the World
The Lone Wolf who became the first range-warden after losing everyone
stereotypes: Savage and territorial
Slaves to instinct (the elders find this laughable)
Can't survive alone (mostly true, and they know it)
rpHooks: You were cast out of your pack and carry the shame of a lone-wolf name
Your pack owes a range-treaty debt that only you can pay
advHooks: The Hunt is riding by daylight and your range is in its path
A rival pack has broken the range-treaty and named your pack for the blame
wolfkin.greeting: A brief touch of foreheads: 'Pack runs on.'
wolfkin.oath: 'By moon and pack, I do not run alone.'
wolfkin.symbol: A howling wolf beneath a full moon

owlkin.origin: Owlkin are the world's watchers, keepers of what happens while everyone else sleeps.
owlkin.homeland: The Emerald Wilds, the Moonlit Vale, and the Frostbound North
owlkin.culture: Great-owls of the deep forest, snow-owls of the north, night-owls of the Vale, ghost-owls of the shadow, sun-owls of the heights. Owlkin cultures prize silence, patience, and knowledge; they are the seers, librarians, and night-sentinels of a dozen realms.
owlkin.society: Roost-orders organized around learning and watch-keeping; elders are those who have simply seen the most.
owlkin.government: Roost-conclaves and seer-circles; decisions are slow and heavily debated.
owlkin.beliefs: The stars, the night, and the sacred duty of the witness. To see and say nothing can be a grave sin or a sacred trust, depending on the roost.
traditions: The Long Watch, a solitary vigil that marks adulthood
Star-reading and dream-augury
The keeping of Witness-books, records of what the roost has seen
owlkin.language: A soft, hooting tongue full of pauses that carry meaning.
owlkin.architecture: High roost-towers and library-spires with wide night-windows.
owlkin.clothing: Muffling feather-cloaks and quiet robes; scholar's greys and night-blues.
owlkin.food: Simple and quiet; the owlkin eat little and think much.
owlkin.military: Silent night-scouts and ambush-archers; owlkin are the eyes of an army, rarely its fist.

relations.kitsune: Vale co-conspirators and rivals in the trade of secrets.
relations.seraphim: Star-readers who look to the same heights.

history: Kept the Witness-books through every age, the closest thing to unbroken history
Watched the sky break and recorded it when others fled
Dream-wardens rose to guard against the Vale's dream-thieves
legends: The Watcher Who Never Slept and saw the first dawn twice
The Lost Witness-book that recorded the Nameless Emperor's true name
stereotypes: Cold and unknowable
Hoarders of secrets
All watching, never acting
rpHooks: Your roost keeps a Witness-book with a page torn out, and you mean to find it
You broke the Long Watch and saw something you were not meant to
advHooks: A dream-thief is stealing from the Vale and your roost sent you to end it
A page from a lost Witness-book surfaces naming your character
owlkin.greeting: A slow blink and a bow: 'Well seen.'
owlkin.oath: 'By star and silence, I bear witness.'
owlkin.symbol: An open eye within a crescent of feathers

tigerkin.origin: Tigerkin are solitary sovereigns, each said to be the ruler of whatever ground they stand on.
tigerkin.homeland: The Emerald Wilds, with lines in the Sunscorch, Stormreach, and Shadowlands
tigerkin.culture: Jungle bengals, white tigers of the cold heights, shadow-tigers of the border, storm-tigers of the coast, ancient-tigers of the old bloodlines. Tigerkin prize independence, personal honor, and single combat; their societies are looser than most beast-kin because a tiger bows to no pack.
tigerkin.society: Territory-holders bound by codes of challenge and hospitality rather than by clans; a tigerkin's word and ground are everything.
tigerkin.government: No thrones; territory-elders arbitrate disputes and honor-challenges.
tigerkin.beliefs: Personal honor as sacred law; the sun for the bengals, the moon for the shadow-lines, the storm for the coast.
traditions: The Claiming, a young tigerkin marking a first territory to earn adulthood
Single-combat challenges to settle honor, rarely to the death
Guest-law: a tigerkin's home is inviolable sanctuary
tigerkin.language: A low, resonant tongue of few words and heavy silences.
tigerkin.architecture: Solitary strongholds and territory-shrines; tigerkin build for one, not many.
tigerkin.clothing: Marked with personal sigils and trophies of honor-duels.
tigerkin.food: Hunted alone and eaten with ceremony; sharing a kill is a deep bond.
tigerkin.military: Elite single combatants and shock-champions; tigerkin do not form lines, they break them.

relations.lionkin: Ancient rivalry of the solitary and the pride; respect edged with disdain.
relations.wolfkin: The lone versus the pack, a philosophical feud.
relations.human: Prized champions and feared duelists in human courts.

history: The ancient-tiger lines claim descent from the First Age's great hunters
White tigers withdrew to the cold heights during the Age of Ash
Shadow-tigers took to the border in the Blood Wars
legends: The Tiger Who Held a Bridge Alone against an army
The First Claiming, a territory said to be the whole world
stereotypes: Arrogant loners
Deadly and vain
Unable to work with others (until they choose to, and then absolutely)
rpHooks: You lost your first territory and wander to reclaim your honor
You owe a life-debt from a guest-law sanctuary you once broke
advHooks: An honor-challenge has followed you across the world and will not end
Your ancient bloodline is said to return in a time of breaking
tigerkin.greeting: A measured nod, claws sheathed and shown: 'Your ground is yours.'
tigerkin.oath: 'By claw and honor, my word holds.'
colors: Ember-orange and black; white and slate for the cold lines
tigerkin.symbol: A single tiger's eye over crossed claws

bearkin.origin: Bearkin are the settled guardians of the wild places, slow to anger and impossible to move.
bearkin.homeland: The Frostbound North and the Ironspine, with lines in the Emerald Wilds
bearkin.culture: Brown-bears of the forest, polar-bears of the ice, black-bears of the hills, cave-bears of the deep, great-bears of the old bloodlines. Bearkin cultures are hearth-centered and protective; they hibernate through the hardest season and wake as the fiercest guardians a community can have.
bearkin.society: Family-holds and guardian-lodges; a bearkin belongs to those they protect, not to a clan.
bearkin.government: Hold-elders and guardian-councils; slow, deliberate, consensus-bound.
bearkin.beliefs: The cycle of sleep and waking, the sanctity of the hearth, and the ancestors who guard from the long sleep.
traditions: The First Winter, a young bearkin's first solitary hibernation-vigil
Hearth-guarding oaths sworn to a family or place
The Waking Feast that ends the winter sleep
bearkin.language: A deep, slow tongue; bearkin famously never waste a word.
bearkin.architecture: Heavy hearth-lodges and cave-holds built to shelter many and outlast storms.
bearkin.clothing: Thick furs and hearth-marks; layered and practical.
bearkin.food: Enormous seasonal feasts before the sleep; foraged, fished, and preserved.
bearkin.military: Immovable defenders and shield-bearers; a roused bearkin holds a doorway against an army.

relations.goliath: Northern kin in temperament; both value patience and strength held in reserve.
relations.wolfkin: Forest-sharers, wary but rarely at war.

history: Guarded the northern holds through the Stormfall's worst winters
The cave-bear lines withdrew into the Ironspine during the Age of Ash
Woke as guardians when the Winter Hunt first crossed south
legends: The Great Bear who slept a hundred years and woke to save a dying hold
The First Winter that lasted an age
stereotypes: Slow and lazy (until roused, and then it is far too late)
Gentle giants
Sleep through every crisis
rpHooks: You woke early from the First Winter to find your hold gone
You are hearth-sworn to protect someone who has left and needs you
advHooks: The Winter Hunt is bearing down on the hold you are sworn to guard
Your great-bear bloodline is said to wake only when the world is breaking
bearkin.greeting: A slow, full embrace: 'Warm hearth to you.'
bearkin.oath: 'By hearth and the long sleep, I guard.'
bearkin.symbol: A bear curled around a hearth-fire

lionkin.origin: Lionkin are the pride-peoples, who believe that no one stands alone and that a crown is only as real as those who kneel and those who rise.
lionkin.homeland: The Sunscorch Desert, with prides in the Crownlands and Stormreach
lionkin.culture: Sun-lions of the desert court, desert-lions of the deep dunes, mountain-lions of the high passes, golden-lions of the old royal lines, dusk-lions of the shadow-border. Lionkin build proud, sun-warmed societies of prides and courts, where loyalty and rulership are the great questions.
lionkin.society: Pride-and-court; a lionkin's worth is measured by the pride they lift and the pride that lifts them. Ambition is respected when it serves the whole.
lionkin.government: Sun-courts and pride-councils; the Sun Court of Sunspire is the grandest.
lionkin.beliefs: The sun as the source of rightful rule; the pride as sacred family; ancestor-kings who watch from the light.
traditions: The Sun-Rite, a coming-of-age at the summer solstice
The Pride-Oath binding a lionkin to defend their court
Golden-mane braiding that marks rank and deed
lionkin.language: A rolling, proud dialect made for oratory and command.
lionkin.architecture: Sun-warmed courts, needle-spires, and open colonnades of gold stone.
lionkin.clothing: Sun-gold and desert-white; manes groomed and ornamented by rank.
lionkin.food: Communal court-feasts; the pride eats together, ruler and hunter alike.
lionkin.military: Coordinated pride-cavalry and champion-led lines; lionkin fight for one another, not for spoils.

relations.tigerkin: Ancient rivals; the pride and the loner will never agree on what strength is for.
relations.seraphim: Both revere the light; sun-court and radiant-choir keep old ties.

history: Founded the Sun Court after the Sunscorch swallowed the old kingdoms
Golden-lion royal lines claim descent from the buried desert empires
Held the oasis-roads open through the Age of Ash
legends: The First Sun-King, crowned by the light itself
The Pride That Would Not Break at the fall of a city
stereotypes: Proud and domineering
Obsessed with rank and rulership
All roar, expecting others to kneel
rpHooks: You are a pride-less lionkin, cast out and seeking a court to call your own
You carry a golden-lion claim to a throne that no longer exists
advHooks: The Sun Court's heir is lost in the deep dunes and your pride is blamed
A buried desert empire's crown surfaces and your bloodline is named
lionkin.greeting: A raised chin and open hand: 'Rise, and be seen.'
lionkin.oath: 'By sun and pride, I hold my court.'
lionkin.symbol: A lion's mane rayed like the sun

birdkin.origin: Birdkin are the most varied of all the beast-kin, a whole sky of peoples who share only wings and the horizon.
birdkin.homeland: Everywhere with sky: the Skyward Isles, the Sapphire Sea coasts, the Crownlands, and beyond
birdkin.culture: There is no single birdkin culture: ravens and crows keep clever, secretive city-guilds; eagles and hawks hold proud highland aeries; sea-birds crew the world's ships; songbirds and cardinals fill the market-quarters with music; vultures keep the solemn death-rites others shun. Each bird-line is nearly its own people.
birdkin.society: Aerie-clans, city-guilds, ship-crews, and roving flocks; birdkin organize by trade and temperament as much as by blood.
birdkin.government: Aerie-councils in the heights, guild-charters in the cities, ship-articles at sea.
birdkin.beliefs: The open sky and the freedom of it; many birdkin honor the wind, the stars, or the ancestors who fly ahead.
traditions: The First Flight, a fledgling's solo crossing to earn adult standing
Flock-songs that carry news and history across great distances
Feather-gifts exchanged to seal bonds and bargains
birdkin.language: A whistling, song-laced Trade-Common that carries far on the wind.
birdkin.clothing: Light and bright, feather-marked by line and deed.
birdkin.food: As varied as the lines: sea-fish, grain, fruit, or the vultures' solemn shares.
birdkin.military: Aerial scouts, sky-cavalry, and cliff-archers; birdkin own the air above any battle.

relations.harengon: Sky-cousins and racing rivals in the Isles.
relations.seraphim: The winged and the wingless-of-heaven share the high air uneasily.
relations.human: Partners in every port and market-quarter.

history: Kept the message-lines open across every scattered region after the Sundering
The sea-bird lines crewed the fleets that mapped the Sapphire Sea
Aerie-clans settled the Skyward Isles when the land first flew
legends: The First Flight that circled the broken world
The Raven Who Stole a King's True Name
stereotypes: Flighty, thieving, gossip-carriers (the raven-lines lean in)
Proud aerie-snobs (the eagle-lines)
Can't be pinned down
rpHooks: You failed your First Flight and have something to prove
Your line keeps a flock-song with a verse no one will explain
advHooks: A message your line carried has sparked a war
A sinking Skyward isle holds your aerie and few lifeboats remain
birdkin.greeting: A brush of the back of the hand, like a passing wing: 'Fair skies.'
birdkin.oath: 'By wind and horizon, I fly true.'
colors: As many as there are birds
birdkin.symbol: A single feather against an open sky

vampire.origin: Vampires are the returned: those who did not stay dead, whether by curse, bargain, bloodline, or the long dark of the Blood Wars.
vampire.homeland: The Shadowlands and the Moonlit Vale, with old houses in the Blackdeep and Abyssal Trench
vampire.culture: Blood-born fledglings, night-born house-scions, crimson warrior-lines, moon-blood mystics, and the truly ancient. Vampire society runs on patience, debt, and the Dusk Accord; not all are villains, and the oldest have seen too many ages to bother with cruelty for its own sake.
vampire.society: House-and-court, bound by centuries-old accords and blood-debts. Age is authority; the young serve, the ancient rule and rarely stir.
vampire.government: The Night Court and its rival houses; law is precedent, and precedent is very, very old.
vampire.beliefs: The long view: that all things pass and the patient inherit. Death-traditions, ancestor-communion, and the Dusk Accord that keeps the peace with the living.
traditions: The Turning-Vigil, the first night of the returned, spent under a house's protection
Blood-accords, binding promises sealed in a drop of blood
The Century-Court, when houses settle debts once every hundred years
vampire.language: Old courtly dialects, several of them dead languages the vampires simply never stopped speaking.
vampire.architecture: Sunless halls, mirror-less courts, and deep house-vaults.
vampire.clothing: Timeless formal wear centuries out of fashion, worn with total confidence.
vampire.food: Blood, given or taken; the Accord governs how, and violating it is the gravest crime.
occupations: Brokers of secrets and old debts
vampire.military: Old, disciplined night-guard and duelists; vampires fight the way they live, patiently and to win.

relations.kitsune: Vale intriguers who trade in the same currency of secrets.
relations.wolfkin: Shadow-border neighbors, wary across a long truce.
relations.seraphim: Ancient opposites of dark and light, bound by an even more ancient wariness.

history: Rose to power during the Blood Wars as the light failed
The Dusk Accord ended the open wars and drew the shadow-border
The oldest houses remember the sky breaking, and keep what they saw to themselves
legends: The First Returned, who bargained back from death and set the Accord
The Ancient who has not woken in three hundred years and whose house waits
stereotypes: Bloodthirsty monsters (the young, sometimes; the old find it gauche)
Scheming aristocrats
All of them evil (the Accord and the war against the Unlit say otherwise)
rpHooks: You are newly returned and do not yet know which house made you
Your house owes a blood-accord your character must honor across the ages
advHooks: The Unlit mean to put out the sun and even your house wants them stopped
An ancient of your house is waking, and no one knows what it will want
vampire.greeting: A slow, formal bow, never offering the throat: 'Long nights.'
vampire.oath: 'By blood and accord, I keep my word past death.'
vampire.symbol: A closed eye above a single drop

seaborn.origin: Seaborn are the peoples of the water, some who always lived below and some who went down when the coasts drowned.
seaborn.homeland: The Sapphire Sea and the Abyssal Trench
seaborn.culture: Tide-born of the shallows, reef-born of the coral cities, deep-born of the cold dark, storm-tide of the tempest coast, abyss-born of the trench, pearl-born of the trade-currents. Seaborn cultures range from bright reef-market societies to the alien, hymn-singing courts of the abyss.
seaborn.society: Current-and-covenant; the Tide Covenant binds many, but the deep and abyssal folk keep their own strange orders.
seaborn.government: The Coral Throne of the covenant above; the abyss-choir and deeper councils below.
seaborn.beliefs: The tides as breath of the world; ancestor-currents that carry the dead out to sea; the abyss-folk keep faiths the surface finds disturbing.
traditions: The First Descent, a young seaborn's dive into deeper water to earn adulthood
Tide-singing that marks births, deaths, and the turning currents
Pearl-gifting to seal bonds and treaties
seaborn.language: A fluid, tonal tongue that carries through water; the abyss-choir sing it in registers the surface cannot hear.
seaborn.architecture: Living coral cities, current-shaped halls, and the vent-lit spires of the deep.
seaborn.clothing: Current-woven kelp-silk and pearl; the deep-folk go bare but for bio-luminous marks.
seaborn.food: Fish, kelp, urchin, and the strange harvests of the vents.
seaborn.military: Undersea raiders and reef-guard; seaborn fight in three dimensions and drag foes down where they cannot follow.

relations.turtlekin: Island-and-reef kin; the covenant and the turtle-elders share long ties.
relations.human: Surface trade-partners and toll-rivals in every port.
relations.vampire: The abyss and the drowned dark share unsettling neighbors.

history: Some descended when the coasts drowned in the Stormfall
The Tide Covenant rose to govern the deep water after the drowning
The abyss-choir emerged from the trench in an age no surface record names
legends: The First Descent that reached the trench floor and came back singing
The Drowned City that was never built by hands from above
stereotypes: Cold and unknowable (the deep-folk especially)
Grasping toll-takers (say the free-captains)
The abyss-born are all cultists (the surface fears what it can't hear)
rpHooks: You were born below and are the first of your current to walk on land
You carry a drowned relic your abyss-kin want returned to the dark
advHooks: The reef-serpents are fleeing something in the deep and driving ashore
The abyss-choir's hymn is being heard in surface harbors and no one knows why
seaborn.greeting: A rippling hand-sign, palm turned like a current: 'Fair tides.'
seaborn.symbol: A spiraling wave around a single pearl

turtlekin.origin: Turtlekin are the long-memoried elders of the islands and rivers, who measure time in tides and think in generations.
turtlekin.homeland: The Sapphire Sea islands, with lines on the rivers and the deep reefs
turtlekin.culture: Shell-guards of the island holds, sea-turtles of the open water, river-backs of the inland waterways, terrapins of the marsh-villages, ancient-shells of the oldest lines. Turtlekin cultures are patient, lawful, and deeply communal; they are the mediators and record-keepers of the sea-peoples.
turtlekin.society: Elder-councils where the oldest shell speaks last and decides most; slow, careful, consensus-bound.
turtlekin.government: Island elder-circles and river-moots; turtlekin are famous neutral arbiters.
turtlekin.beliefs: The long tide, the sanctity of the given word, and the ancestors carried in the shell. Patience is the highest virtue.
traditions: The Shell-Marking, a life-record carved slowly into one's own shell over decades
The Elder-Circle, where disputes are heard across many days
The keeping of tide-law, treaties turtlekin memorize for all parties
turtlekin.language: A slow, deliberate tongue; a turtlekin sentence can take a while and always means exactly what it says.
turtlekin.architecture: Low, storm-proof island holds and stilt-villages built to endure centuries.
turtlekin.clothing: Simple and marked with shell-sigils; turtlekin adorn the shell, not the body.
turtlekin.food: Sea-greens, shellfish, and slow-cooked communal stews.
turtlekin.military: Immovable island-guard; a turtlekin shield-line simply does not break, and they are content to wait out any siege.

relations.seaborn: Reef-and-island kin; turtle elders often arbitrate covenant disputes.
relations.human: Trusted neutral parties in port-town law.
relations.halfling: Fellow small, underestimated, community-first folk who get along famously.

history: Kept the tide-law that let the sea-peoples trade after the Stormfall
Their ancient-shell elders are living records older than most kingdoms
Mediated the treaties that made Port Meridian a free port
legends: The Ancient Shell who remembers the First Age and speaks of it once a century
The Elder Who Outwaited a War
stereotypes: Impossibly slow
Stubborn and unmovable
Boring (until you need a fair judge, and then there is no one better)
rpHooks: You are a young turtlekin who left before your Shell-Marking was complete
Your elder-circle entrusted you with a tide-law treaty to deliver intact
advHooks: A tide-law treaty you carry could stop or start a reef-war
Your island hold sits above something the Deep Conclave wants sealed
turtlekin.greeting: A slow bow with both hands on the chest: 'Long tides carry you.'
turtlekin.oath: 'By shell and tide-law, my word endures.'
turtlekin.symbol: A carved shell ringed with tide-marks

kitsune.origin: Kitsune are the shapers of story and secret, whose oldest lines are said to grow a new tail with each age of cunning survived.
kitsune.homeland: The Moonlit Vale and the Shadowlands
kitsune.culture: Red-tails of the courts and markets, silver-tails of the old noble lines, shadow-tails of the border, frost-tails of the cold Vale, sun-tails of the rare bright days, and the whispered void-tails. Kitsune build cultures of intrigue, art, and favor; a kitsune's greatest weapon and worst danger is the debt owed and the story told.
kitsune.society: Court-and-favor; status is a web of debts, secrets, and reputations. Nothing is owned so much as owed.
kitsune.government: The Moon Court, ruled by masks, favors, and whoever holds the most dangerous secrets.
kitsune.beliefs: The moon, the mask, and the sacred weight of a promise; to a kitsune, a favor freely given is a bond stronger than any chain.
traditions: The First Mask, a coming-of-age when a young kitsune is given, or takes, their court-face
Favor-debts, tracked with absolute precision and never forgiven, only repaid
Tale-telling contests where reputations are made and unmade
kitsune.language: A layered, allusive dialect where the second meaning matters more than the first.
kitsune.architecture: Silk-walled salons, mirror-halls, and the shifting paths of the Turning Wood.
kitsune.clothing: Exquisite masks, moon-silk, and layered robes that conceal as much as they display.
kitsune.food: Delicate, artful, and ceremonial; a kitsune meal is a conversation.
kitsune.military: Rarely open war; kitsune fight with illusion, misdirection, and the ruin of reputations. Their few soldiers are masked infiltrators.

relations.harengon: Vale co-conspirators; a kitsune and a harengon scheme is a beautiful, dangerous thing.
relations.vampire: Fellow players of the long game of secrets.
relations.owlkin: Rivals and partners in the trade of what is known.

history: Kept the Moonlit Vale independent through intrigue when armies failed
The silver-tail houses are older than the Sundering they quietly survived
Rose as brokers between the living and the night-courts after the Blood Wars
legends: The Nine-Tailed One who owns a favor from everyone who ever lived
The Tale That Toppled a Throne with no army at all
stereotypes: Tricksters and liars (they prefer 'storytellers')
Never to be trusted
All schemes, no loyalty (yet a repaid favor is sacred)
rpHooks: You owe a favor-debt you cannot repay and cannot escape
You took a court-mask that belonged to someone who wants it back
advHooks: A kitsune noble's favor has made your character a piece in a Moon Court game
One of the Nine Lanterns has gone out and your house is blamed
kitsune.greeting: A masked bow and a knowing smile: 'What a story you must have.'
kitsune.oath: 'By moon and mask, a favor owed is a favor kept.'
kitsune.symbol: A fox-mask beneath a crescent, with many tails

seraphim.origin: Seraphim are the winged folk of the high places, descended from those who dwelt near the broken sky and did not fully fall.
seraphim.homeland: The Celestial Heights and the Skyward Isles
seraphim.culture: Dawn-wings of first light, star-born of the constellations' service, radiant orthodoxy of the choir, high-wings of the drifting isles, and the astral seers of the Threshold. Seraphim cultures are luminous and rigid, torn between the choir's orthodoxy and the Fallen who chose the ground and its freedoms.
seraphim.society: Choir-and-order, deeply hierarchical, structured by proximity to the light. The great schism is between the Radiant Choir and the Fallen Covenant.
seraphim.government: The Radiant Choir and the Star Court above; the Fallen keep looser, exiled communities below.
seraphim.beliefs: The star-fire and the sanctity of the sky; a duty to guard the Threshold and prevent the sky breaking again. The Fallen believe the light must be lived among mortals, not hoarded above them.
traditions: The Ascension-Rite, a young seraph's first climb to the Threshold
Star-song devotions timed to the constellations
The Choosing, when a seraph may keep the Heights or become Fallen and take the ground
seraphim.language: Celestial, a resonant, chiming tongue said to be half-song.
seraphim.architecture: Star-glass halls, radiant spires, and the impossible geometries of the Heights.
seraphim.clothing: Light-woven robes and star-glass ornaments; the Fallen dress plainly among mortals.
seraphim.food: Little and luminous above; the Fallen learn mortal fare and mostly enjoy it.
occupations: Fallen healers, teachers, and wanderers among mortals
seraphim.military: Radiant guardians and light-wardens; seraphim fight rarely and terribly, wielding star-fire against the dark.

relations.vampire: Ancient opposites; light and dark bound by wary old accords.
relations.genasi: Kindred of the upper realms who share the high, thin air.
relations.owlkin: Fellow star-readers, respected across the schism.
relations.the-unlit: Sworn enemies; the Unlit would put out the very light seraphim guard.

history: Their line dates from the War of Broken Skies, when the sky first broke
The first Fallen chose the ground during that war and were exiled
The Choir's schism deepens over a forbidden prophecy of a second breaking
legends: The First Fallen, who traded the Heights for a single mortal life and never regretted it
The Prophecy the Choir Forbids, said to name the sky's second breaking
stereotypes: Serene and holy (the Choir cultivates it)
Judgmental and cold
All of them good (the Choir's rigidity and the Fallen's heresy both complicate that)
rpHooks: You are Fallen, exiled from the Heights for choosing the ground
The Choir's records name your character in a prophecy they mean to silence
advHooks: The stars over the Threshold are going out and the Choir is fracturing
A Fallen asks you to carry a message the Choir has forbidden
seraphim.greeting: A touch of two fingers to the brow, then up: 'Light keep you.'
seraphim.oath: 'By star-fire and the Threshold, I hold the sky.'
seraphim.symbol: A rayed star between two wings

goliath.origin: Goliath are the giant-blooded of the high and hard places, who believe the mountains test the worthy and remember the failures.
goliath.homeland: The Ironspine Mountains and the Frostbound North
goliath.culture: Stone-blooded of the peaks, frost-blooded of the north, storm-blooded of the tempest heights, mountain-born clans, and the rare titan-born of the oldest lines. Goliath cultures are honor-bound and competitive in the best sense: they measure themselves against the mountain, not against the weak.
goliath.society: Clan-and-crossing; standing is earned through trials, the greatest being the Crossing of Nine Bridges. A goliath keeps a fair tally of their own deeds and expects the same of others.
goliath.government: Clan-moots and the High Clans confederation; leadership is trial-earned and provisional.
goliath.beliefs: The mountain as impartial judge, the storm as a test, and ancestors who watch from the high stones. Fairness is sacred; a rigged contest is the deepest shame.
traditions: The Crossing of Nine Bridges, the great coming-of-age pilgrimage above the cloud line
The Fair Tally, an honest reckoning of one's own deeds and failures
The Stone-Bell rite, ringing a household bell said to be forged from a first survivor's armor
goliath.language: A resonant, echoing highland tongue built to carry across peaks.
goliath.architecture: Fortress-holds cut into mountainsides and sky-bridges strung above the clouds.
goliath.clothing: Stone-grey wraps and clan-marks; heavy furs in the north.
goliath.food: Hardy mountain fare, sky-goat, glacier-fish, and trial-feasts.
goliath.military: Elite mountain infantry and champions; goliath fight fair, hit like an avalanche, and never claim a victory they did not earn.

relations.dwarf: Peak-and-root neighbors; rivals for the mountains, partners against the deep dark.
relations.orc: Highland kin in honor-code and strength.
relations.bearkin: Northern kin in patience and guardianship.

history: Kept the high passes and sky-bridges through every age
The Crossing of Nine Bridges predates the Old Empire
Titan-born lines are said to descend from the giants of the First Age
legends: The First Survivor of the Skyfall, whose armor became the first Storm-Bell
The Titan-Born who held a bridge until the mountain itself gave way
stereotypes: Grim and humorless (they are simply serious about fairness)
All brawn
Obsessed with pointless trials (the trials are the point)
rpHooks: You failed your Crossing of Nine Bridges and wander to earn your standing
Your household Storm-Bell has cracked, an ill omen you must answer
advHooks: A vault-claim dispute is about to turn your clan-moot into a clan war
The Crossing has grown deadly and something is picking off the young on the bridges
goliath.greeting: A firm clasp of the forearm, deed for deed: 'Fair stone to you.'
goliath.oath: 'By the mountain's fair judgment, I earn my place.'

goblin.origin: Goblins are the survivors and scavengers who thrive where the great peoples cannot, and who are far cleverer than the great peoples like to admit.
goblin.homeland: The Blackdeep, the Ashen Wastes, and the underside of every city
goblin.culture: Cave-goblins of the Deep, scrap-goblins of the salvage-yards, night-goblins of the shadow, redcaps of the old blood-rites, and moss-goblins of the quiet wilds. Goblin cultures prize cleverness, community, and making much from little; not all are wicked, and the redcaps' fearsome reputation is a story most goblins resent.
goblin.society: Warren-and-crew; survival is collective, and a good idea from anyone is worth more than a title. Goblins share what they scavenge or the warren fails.
goblin.government: Warren-councils and crew-bosses chosen for cleverness, not strength.
goblin.beliefs: The luck of the overlooked, the spirits of scrap and stone, and the old, darker rites the redcaps keep. Cleverness is a kind of prayer.
traditions: The First Find, a young goblin's rite of building something useful from pure scrap
Warren-sharing, where hoarding from the crew is the gravest crime
The Redcaps' old blood-rites, feared and misunderstood even among goblins
goblin.language: A fast, slangy, invention-rich tongue full of borrowed words and coined ones.
goblin.architecture: Ingenious warren-tunnels, scrap-forts, and hidden Deep-cities lit by glowcap.
goblin.clothing: Patchwork, pocketed, and cleverly made from whatever the great folk threw away.
goblin.food: Resourceful and communal; goblins can make a feast from a famine.
goblin.military: Traps, tunnels, ambush, and clever devices; goblins never fight fair because fighting fair is how the small die.

relations.halfling: Two overlooked small peoples who get on famously.
relations.dwarf: Old prejudice, though the forge-cities quietly run on goblin labor.
relations.orc: Ash-clan and cave-goblin share the Wastes uneasily but honestly.

history: Survived every catastrophe by being beneath notice and quick to adapt
Kept the Sunless Market and the smuggling-lines running in the dark ages
Redcaps' reputation dates to a blood-war the other lines refuse to own
legends: The Tinker Who Built a City from a Scrapheap
The First Find that turned out to be a fallen star
stereotypes: Wicked, thieving, and cowardly (mostly slander)
Redcaps are all murderers (a story goblins hate)
Too dim to matter (a fatal underestimation)
rpHooks: You built something from scrap that a powerful person now wants back
You left the warren rather than take part in a redcap rite
advHooks: Something is coming up through the Deepest Door your Deep-warren guards
A device you built has fallen into the wrong hands and must be recovered
goblin.greeting: A quick showing of empty, then busy, hands: 'What've we got, then?'
goblin.oath: 'By luck and the warren, I share and I survive.'
goblin.symbol: A cog wound with a lucky knot

genasi.origin: Genasi carry a living piece of the elemental realms, and where that element runs strongest shapes a wholly different people.
genasi.homeland: The Elemental Marches and the Stormreach
genasi.culture: Flame-born of the fire-realm's edge, tide-born of the living waters, stone-born of the deep earth, wind-born of the high air, storm-born of the tempest, frost-born of the elemental cold. Genasi cluster by element, and each element carries its own temper, art, and philosophy, so that a flame-born and a tide-born share only the fact of being part-elemental.
genasi.society: Element-pact communities on the frontier of the Marches, each bound to and wary of the realm in their blood.
genasi.government: Elemental-pact councils and the marchwarden orders that watch them.
genasi.beliefs: The element as both gift and danger; many genasi tend shrines to their realm, some to worship it, some to keep it at bay. The element is a relationship, not a fate.
traditions: The First Kindling, when a young genasi's elemental nature fully wakes
Element-tending, the daily care of a shrine or spring tied to one's realm
The Pact-Renewal, reaffirming the bargain that keeps a community's element in balance
genasi.language: Trade-Common laced with elemental cant, each element with its own dialect and idiom.
genasi.architecture: Element-shaped: flame-forges, water-halls, floating-stone holds, storm-spires.
genasi.clothing: Element-marked and practical; flame-born favor ember-cloth, tide-born flowing weaves.
genasi.food: Element-touched fare, from ember-seared to spring-chilled.
occupations: Smiths, healers, and artisans of their element
genasi.military: Elemental adepts and pact-champions; a storm-born line and a stone-born line wage war in completely different ways.

relations.dragonborn: Kindred elemental-blooded folk; sometimes allies, sometimes rivals for the same realms.
relations.seraphim: Wind and storm genasi share the high realms with the winged.
relations.goliath: Stone-born and stone-blooded find easy kinship.

history: Settled the Elemental Marches when the rifts first opened
The pact-communities have kept the elements from spilling inland for ages
Storm-born lines trace to the Stormfall, frost-born to the drowning cold
legends: The First Kindling, a spark drawn straight from the elemental realm
The Pact-Keeper who held a rift closed with their own body
stereotypes: All of them spellcasters (false; many never wield their element as a weapon)
Cold, hot-headed, or aloof depending on the element
Not quite people (an old and cruel prejudice)
rpHooks: Your element kindled wrong, in a realm that is not your line's
You are pact-bound to tend a shrine you fled
advHooks: The Standing Rift is widening and your pact is failing to hold it
An elemental-pact offered your character power for a price you must now pay or refuse
genasi.greeting: A palm briefly kindled with one's element and shown: 'Balance to you.'
genasi.oath: 'By the element I carry and keep in balance, I hold.'
colors: By element: flame-red, tide-blue, stone-ochre, wind-white, storm-violet, frost-cyan
genasi.symbol: A ring of the six elemental sigils
